target.title: fix(agents): preserve fresh tool results during aggregate recovery
target.body:
"## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99481.

Tool-result aggregate recovery can erase a fresh tool result when the session already has a frozen projection baseline and a runtime/context message follows the new result. That matches the observed failure mode where deterministic stdout probes such as `printf`, `echo`, `python print`, and `node console.log` were rendered back to the agent as `(no output)` after prior tool-result truncation activity.

The key failure is not that the command produced no output. The command may produce output, but the current tool-result text can be reduced away while older projected history is being compacted to satisfy the aggregate prompt budget.

## Implementation

- Track whether the tool-result projection state already has a frozen baseline.
- Mark newly seen projection entries as protected from aggregate recovery once a frozen baseline exists.
- Keep existing protection for trailing tool results.
- Preserve the existing fallback behavior for oversized fresh batches, so budget recovery can still trim when the fresh batch itself exceeds the aggregate budget.

## Regression Coverage

Adds a focused regression test that:

- Builds saturated historical tool-result output.
- Freezes the projection baseline with an initial truncation pass.
- Appends a fresh small tool result followed by a runtime-context-like user message.
- Verifies the fresh output remains visible while total aggregate tool-result text stays within budget.

## Validation

Local lightweight checks:

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` passed: 43 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-embedded-agent.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` passed: 43 tests.

I did not run the full local matrix. Please rely on PR CI / GitHub Actions for broader target validation.

## Risk

Low to medium. The change is scoped to tool-result truncation candidate selection. It makes aggregate recovery prefer older projected history over newly added tool results after a frozen projection baseline exists. The main risk is preserving more fresh output may require more reduction from older entries, but the aggregate budget check remains enforced and oversized fresh batches still have fallback trimming coverage.

## Notes

I attempted to update issue #99481 directly with the Linux reproduction evidence and root-cause direction, but the bot account does not have `UpdateIssue` permission on `openclaw/openclaw`. The additional evidence is therefore included here in the PR body.
"
